questions.question: You create a subnet that uses the address range 10.10.4.0/27. How many IP addresses in the subnet can be assigned to virtual machines?

options.why: Correct. A /27 contains 32 addresses, and Azure reserves 5 addresses in every subnet.
This assumes only the network and broadcast addresses are reserved. Azure reserves 5 addresses.
Azure reserves 5 of the 32 addresses for the network, default gateway, Azure DNS and broadcast.
Azure reserves 5 addresses, not 3.

questions.explanation: Azure reserves the network address, the default gateway (.1), two addresses for Azure DNS (.2 and .3) and the broadcast address in each subnet.

questions.question: You plan to peer VNet1 and VNet2 and to connect both to an on-premises network that uses 192.168.0.0/16. VNet1 uses 10.1.0.0/16. Which address space can you use for VNet2?

options.why: Correct. It does not overlap VNet1 or the on-premises network.
This range is inside 10.1.0.0/16 and overlaps VNet1, so the peering would fail.
This range overlaps the on-premises network.
This range contains 10.1.0.0/16 and overlaps VNet1.

questions.explanation: Peered virtual networks and connected on-premises networks must use address spaces that do not overlap.

questions.question: You need to create a public IP address for a VPN gateway. The address must not change and must remain available if one availability zone fails. Which configuration should you use?

options.why: Correct. Standard public IP addresses are static and can be zone-redundant.
Basic SKU public IP addresses are retired, and a dynamic address can change.
Standard public IP addresses support only static assignment, and a single zone does not survive a zone failure.
Basic SKU public IP addresses are retired and did not support availability zones.

questions.explanation: Standard SKU public IP addresses are always static and are zone-redundant by default in regions that have availability zones.

questions.question: A virtual machine has a Standard SKU public IP address associated with its network interface. Neither the network interface nor its subnet has a network security group. Users cannot connect to the VM on TCP port 443. What should you do?

options.text: Associate a network security group that allows inbound TCP 443 with the subnet or the network interface
options.why: Correct. Standard public IP addresses are secure by default and block inbound traffic until an NSG allows it.

options.text: Change the public IP address assignment to dynamic
options.why: Standard public IP addresses support only static assignment, and the assignment does not affect filtering.

options.text: Add a DNS name label to the public IP address
options.why: A DNS name label provides a name. It does not allow inbound traffic.

options.text: Change the routing preference to Internet
options.why: Routing preference affects how traffic travels, not whether inbound traffic is allowed.

questions.explanation: Standard SKU public IP addresses are closed to inbound traffic by default. An NSG on the subnet or NIC must explicitly allow the traffic.

questions.question: Which two statements about Azure virtual networks are true? Each correct answer presents a complete solution.

options.text: A virtual network is created in a single Azure region.
options.why: Correct. Use peering to connect virtual networks in different regions.

options.text: A subnet can span all availability zones in its region.
options.why: Correct. Subnets are regional, so zone-redundant resources can share one subnet.

options.text: The smallest supported IPv4 subnet is /30.
options.why: The smallest supported IPv4 subnet is /29.

options.text: A virtual network can span two subscriptions.
options.why: A virtual network belongs to one subscription. Use peering to connect subscriptions.

questions.explanation: A virtual network is scoped to one region and one subscription, while its subnets span the availability zones of that region.
